text.extensions-ipc.ts: Registers the Skills panel's extensions channels (load, save, move between scopes, create a skill, skill linker, import a list) on the workspace sender, running project-scope writes behind the ignore guard and syncing delegate permissions after a linker or list change
text.extensions.ts: Reads and writes the per-user extensions config and the project's own .claude/lantern-extensions.json (the three slots only, written atomically inside the project's .claude folder, a damaged or unsafe file named and ignored without touching the other, a linked worktree resolving to its main checkout) for the Skills panel, saving to the global or the project scope and moving a skill between them with the destination written first, refusing an unknown slot, a locked skill, a bad or repeated name and a damaged file with a catalogue message, and drops a locked skill found in the file on read and on save, keeps the per-slot off list of switchable built-in skills (refusing a locked, foreign or repeated name, dropping one found in the file) and answers the panel with the slots, the always-on, switchable and switched-off skills of each slot, the locked list, the installed skills, the skill linker path, whether that path is initialized, not set or invalid, why it is invalid, how many skills and roles the linker's repo holds and the refusal text. text.explains.ts: Lists and removes saved Markdown explanations in a project's local data folder.
text.filecontent.ts: Reads bounded project text previews after path containment checks and issues provenance for complete source text.
text.hook-cleanup.ts: Removes hook commands that Lantern owns from a Claude settings file, keeping other hooks and writing a timestamped backup first, and runs legacy cleanups one by one.
text.hook-cleanup.ts gotcha: A settings file that does not parse throws instead of being overwritten.
text.hooks.ts: Removes the legacy monitor event hooks, recognized by the Lantern endpoint, from the Claude settings file.
text.lantern-batch.ts: Maps asynchronous work in bounded batches while preserving input order.
text.lantern-cache.ts: Caches parsed file contents by modification time and size, pruning untouched entries after a scoped pass.
text.lantern-describe-parse.ts: Reads the describe lines of a PR record into what, before, after and verified texts, dropping a bad line, stripping comment markers and cost-block or table lines, and capping each text and each section.
text.lantern-enumerate.ts: Enumerates mappable project files using ignore rules, bundled-file markers, size limits, and cached binary and generated-file checks.
text.lantern-flow-parse.ts: Reads the flow lines of a PR record into stories of kinded steps with the record files each step points at, checking kinds, lengths, counts and that every referenced file is one the record lists, and keeping the first problem.
text.lantern-git.ts: Runs bounded Git commands with repository override variables removed and fetches origin with pruning.
text.lantern-host-account.ts: Looks up the project's selected account of a code host through the auth injection and returns its token, with the email for Bitbucket, or nothing when no account resolves or a variable is missing.
text.lantern-host-drivers.ts: Holds one driver per code host that says which git states are asked about (GitHub every one, Bitbucket all but merged), where its credentials come from and how its pull request is requested, and tells whether a record's URL belongs to a host.
text.lantern-host-github.ts: Asks GitHub for one pull request's state, base branch and details (author, created and updated dates, issue plus review comment count, draft flag, requested reviewers without verdicts) with a bearer token, a short timeout and no redirect off the API origin, mapping closed to merged or declined, and tells a rate limit apart from other failures.
text.lantern-host-credentials.ts: Reads the Bitbucket email and API token from the environment, then the project's .ai/.env, skipping a symlinked, oversized or unreadable file and keeping only those two keys, and shares its bounded file reader and line grammar.
text.lantern-host-origin.ts: Reads the origin URL and, through ssh -G for an alias, tells whether the project is on GitHub or Bitbucket, including GitHub's port 443 ssh host, and which owner and repository it is, and keeps the Bitbucket workspace lookup the pull request status started with.
text.lantern-host-request.ts: Asks Bitbucket for one pull request's state, destination branch and details (author, created and updated dates, comment and task counts, draft flag, reviewers with their approvals or change requests) with Basic auth, a short timeout and no redirect off the API origin, mapping OPEN, DECLINED, SUPERSEDED and MERGED, and offers the redirect-safe, size-capped request and the well-formed field readers that the GitHub request reuses.
text.lantern-host-status.ts: Detects the project's code host and caches that host's answers per project and pull request with a TTL, asks in small parallel batches the pull requests its driver names with their avatars inlined, pauses a project for the cache window after a rate limit, and lets the host answer override the git state, with the base branch it reports and the host's pull request details, plus one note when the host cannot be asked; a changed review verdict or update time counts as new data.
text.lantern-ignore.ts: Loads ignore patterns and compiles ordered glob rules for matching project paths.
text.lantern-macro-areas-read.ts: Reads the areas file and turns it into the optional areas part of the macro payload, or one warning line when the file has errors, and nothing when there is no file.
text.lantern-macro-areas.ts: Derives the two-level areas view from the map: area nodes with the foundation band and To assign, area links with main links, foundation links, platforms, the platforms whose files only reach a node through relations, outside systems, and per area its features, edges, stubs to other areas and systems.
text.lantern-macro-files.ts: Names the macro block each shipped file belongs to, using deriveMacroView on one record at a time so the names always match the blocks the view counts.
text.lantern-macro-foundation.ts: Picks the derived edges that touch a foundation block, counts the files of a node on each platform, and counts per node the relations of each platform's files that reach it where the platform has no file, for the areas view.
text.lantern-macro-hint.ts: Decides whether a map with more than 120 records and at least 8 features, and no areas or areas warning, gets the hint that it can be grouped into areas.
text.lantern-macro-load.ts: Serves the macro view with the feature purpose texts of the chosen language, the block and the outside systems of every shipped file and, when the project has an areas file, the areas view or a warning, to a trusted window only for a registered project, returning an error result for a bad project, a missing map or a failed read.
text.lantern-macro-systems.ts: Lists, for each shipped file that talks to an outside system, the systems with how many relations it has to each, so the macro view can narrow the outside systems list to one file.
text.lantern-macro.ts: Derives feature blocks, the edges between them and external systems from parsed map records.
text.lantern-nodes.ts: Builds localized graph nodes and relations from parsed map records, freshness, and platform assignments.
text.lantern-parse.ts: Parses Lantern map records, notes, feature markers and relation arrows with encoded path helpers.
text.lantern-plan-state.ts: Writes a plan section's lines back in canonical form, hashes them into a digest, and derives approval states and item statuses from pull requests through a rule table.
text.lantern-plan-types.ts: Defines the typed plan: its sections, stages with items and questions (each with its touches, explanation and flow), impact, approvals and the parse result, with its kinds and states derived from the skill's format constants.
text.lantern-plan-view-types.ts: Defines what the renderer draws of a plan: its stages in order, items with status and the pull requests that tick them, questions with their touches, explanation and flow, blocked flags and one approval mark per section.
text.lantern-plan-view.ts: Turns a parsed plan and the pull requests the app already derives into the plan view, reading item status, approval marks and a stale plan through the existing reader and counting what is implemented.
text.lantern-plan-fix.ts: Builds the prompt for an agent that fixes a plan file from the problems or the parse error the file has now, and lists the only tools that run may use: reading the map and planning skills, editing that one plan file and running the plan check.
text.lantern-plans.ts: Reads every plan file of the checked-out branch next to the map, hands each to the view builder and reports a file that cannot be read as a warning, and as a broken plan with its file and error, instead of a plan.
text.lantern-plan.ts: Parses a plan file into a typed plan line by line with the scripts' rules, constants and messages (a question's flow through the shared flow reader), skipping unknown tags, refusing stray lines and reporting what it dropped.
text.lantern-platforms.ts: Loads platform glob rules, assigns paths by first match, and builds localized platform summaries.
text.lantern-pr-remote.ts: Lists origin branches and scans recent ones for PR records using bounded parallel Git reads and blob caching.
text.lantern-pr-revisions.ts: Resolves PR before-and-after revisions from branch merge bases, merge parents, or recorded head fallbacks, falls back from a deleted base to the host's base and the default line for an open PR, lists the branches a person may choose between, says why a declined PR cannot be read, and keeps the revisions of a PR on the cached load so later file reads do not work them out again.
text.lantern-sections.ts: Loads localized facts, state machines, database models, and access matrices while validating item references and citations.
text.lantern-stamp.ts: Computes a metadata stamp from Lantern files, leaving out the app's local project data, Git refs, including linked-worktree common refs, and the host-status version.
text.lantern-areas.ts: Reads the optional .lantern/areas tree of areas and their feature ids, with the area descriptions, and reports syntax problems as warnings.
text.lantern-texts.ts: Loads language tables and feature descriptions, chooses the primary language, and tracks translation fallback keys.
text.lantern.ts: Loads cached localized graph data, the plans next to the map with the plan files that cannot be read, independent source coverage and the macro view of the blocks with their feature purpose texts, the block of each file and the outside systems of each file, with bounded project caches and coalesced refresh requests; a fetch of the remote also warms the pull request data in the background.
text.main.ts: Pins the app name and the user-data folder to Lantern before anything reads them, so the package name never moves users' data. Starts the editor server, and so asks for the Microsoft VS Code server licence in a native dialog, only when the Editor is first requested through the Editor switch, New window or Retry (the ws:need-editor and ws:restart-editor channels), never at startup, when a workspace or project window opens, or on scans. Registers the Skills panel's extensions channels, with a native file picker for the import list and the open project's delegate permission rules synced after a linker or import change. Bootstraps the Electron app, tray and application menu (rebuilt when the keymap changes, each item running its command in the workspace window), dispatches command shortcuts in every trusted window, routes second launches and the --project and --compare flags to project windows, scans Claude and Codex sessions, shows a notification when a project's local data cannot be moved, and serves trusted IPC for tools, maps, local comparisons and their reasons, the macro view, previews, providers, user settings, memory sampling, freeing a project's editor memory, the Diagnostics log (started once the single-instance lock is held, every IPC handler wrapped so a failure is recorded, a normal quit marked) with its view, copy and GitHub report channels, RTK status, semantic highlighting, and the explain-a-pull-request-file start, cancel and saved channels with their completion push. A dev run gets a data folder per worktree, seeded from the shared dev one, a tray icon tinted in the build's colour with a short title and a tooltip naming it, a dock badge, its own credential socket, the ports it listens on written to out/lantern-instance.json (with CCM_DEBUG, the debug harness token goes into that file, or into lantern-debug.json in the data folder for the installed profile, and is never printed), and the app:dev-instance channel for the renderer's banner, gates every notification on the notification switch, feeds the overlay its per-kind sound, timing, animation, placement and follow-cursor settings, reads each session's transcript tail to describe its card, maps Codex notices onto the same card shape, opens the tray icon's popover on macOS with the project groups, Clear finished, a test card per kind and Quit (right-click gives a compact native menu, other platforms keep the full native menu), pushes it every refresh, and does not install the lantern command or Codex hooks. The cli:status and cli:install channels use the macOS link installer on macOS and the per-user installer on Linux and Windows. It creates the account store and answers its channels for adding a pasted token, renaming, expiry, status, project, bind, unbind and remove, pushing changes to the trusted windows, gives each agent run the accounts bound to its project, and serves the same accounts on request over a local credential socket that it closes on quit. It sends a card's terminal button to jumpToSession, falling back to opening the project when no terminal is found, and offers deliverTransitionCard the canJumpToSession check. It answers the mic:fix channel by showing a native warning and patching the Claude extension's voice guard only when the user confirms; nothing patches it at start-up or on a timer. It answers the project:ident channel with the app bar's project name, branch and linked-worktree name, only for a registered project. The languages for map runs and explainers come from the language.map and language.explainers settings, resolved per project for set-up, agent runs, settling and one-shot explanations. It warms a project's pull request data when the project opens and answers the channels that refresh that data (fetch, drop the cache and reload) and that revalidate it when a pull request is entered. In an installed build it starts the updater, which checks for a newer release when the update switch is on and, with the session guard fed from the watched sessions, Lantern's own runs and the process list, installs a downloaded update only when nothing would be ended; it answers the update notice channels, pushes the notice to every trusted window, asks for confirmation naming what a Restart now would end, and runs the Check for Updates item. On Windows and Linux it quits through the normal quit path when the last window closes unless a tray icon the user can reach exists, and never while a quit is already running; macOS keeps running.

text.popout.ts: Opens and tracks detached tool windows using the workspace renderer, remembers which window opened each, tells whether a window is one of them, and closes them with their opener, giving the window the Lantern icon on Linux.
text.pr-explain-prompt.ts: Holds the fixed instructions that ask for a JSON answer with a summary, before, after and example, each at most three sentences, builds the prompt from the change, title, reason and other paths with a size cut, and cleans and caps the reply.
text.pr-explain-request.ts: Accepts an explain request only for a registered project, a numeric pull request id and a safe path, then resolves the open or merged pull request and checks the path is one of its files.
text.pr-explain-sections.ts: Reads the agent's JSON reply into summary, before, after and example sections, fills Before for a new file, and falls back to one plain text block when the reply is not valid or complete.
text.pr-explain-store.ts: Keeps one explanation per pull request and file in the app's own data per project, with its sections under a format version when it has them, tagged with the head commit it was written for, marks it stale for another head, and drops the oldest past the entry and size limits.
text.pr-explain.ts: Runs one explanation per file at a time, loads the file's change, turns the reply into sections, saves it under the pull request head, logs its usage and tells the window when it is done or cancelled.
text.prockill.ts: Inspects process trees and port listeners, then terminates a tree or an exact list of pids with graceful and forced cleanup, refusing pid 1 or lower and taking an injectable signal function.
text.dev-instance.ts: Gives a dev build of a worktree its name, its key and its colour, copies the shared dev settings into the build's own data folder once, and writes the build's ports, folder and debug harness token to out/lantern-instance.json, or to lantern-debug.json in the data folder for the installed profile, both owner-only.
text.proctree.ts: Parses process snapshots, traverses descendants, and classifies VS Code server port owners, whether launched by serve-web or directly, for safe reclamation; a serve-web whose launcher is still alive counts as another app's, not stale.
text.projectroot.ts: Resolves session directories to opened projects or owning Git checkouts, including linked and Claude worktrees, names the checkout a chosen folder belongs to, and reads a checkout's current branch and linked-worktree name from its Git files.
text.provider.ts: Defines the Claude and Codex providers, their labels and skill folders, and the session id check.
text.projects.ts: Persists opened and hidden projects, stamps each opening into the project's local data folder, lists roots that have their own window while it is open without saving them, groups sessions, each with its provider, by resolved root, shows a placeholder unavailable session for Claude projects while polling fails, and derives project attention state.

text.serveweb-parse.ts: Classifies VS Code server pages and CLI progress lines into startup phases and percentages.
text.serveweb-code-paths.ts: Lists where the VS Code command may be installed on macOS, Windows and Linux (deb, rpm, snap, flatpak, tarball, PATH) from the platform, home folder and environment, and picks the first one an injected existence check accepts.
text.serveweb-port.ts: Chooses the loopback port for the editor server: the preferred one when free, the previous fallback while it stays free, else any free port.
text.serveweb-port.ts gotcha: On macOS a loopback bind succeeds while another app holds the port on all interfaces, so held ports are not retried.
text.serveweb-probe.ts: Fetches the loopback editor page with a timeout and classifies its readiness through a single callback.
text.serveweb-reclaim.ts: Classifies the editor port owner and reclaims only a stale VS Code server tree before waiting for the port to clear.
text.serveweb-settings.ts: Merges the trust, TypeScript memory cap (under both the unified js/ts and old typescript keys) and delegate-worktree exclusion settings into the embedded editor's settings.json, keeping user values and skipping unparseable files.
text.serveweb-settings.ts gotcha: Never creates either watchOptions key: an object replaces the default "vscode" watcher.
text.serveweb.ts: Owns the embedded VS Code server lifecycle, finds the VS Code command in its usual install locations on each platform, starts nothing until the licence is accepted (asking only when told the start is an open, a decline ending in the retryable error), installs extensions, offers the speech-support patch of the Claude extension for a caller to run on request (never at start-up), and runs it on a free port (preferring a different one for a dev run), started directly with a short grace time or through serve-web when that fails, and reports bounded startup progress and failures with the server output, exposing the pid of the server it started. Every failed start, non-zero exit or stop signal, launch error, stderr line and health-check timeout is also handed to the Diagnostics log with the command that was run.
text.serveweb.ts > src/main/diagnostics/edito: describes why the server stopped, with its exit code, signal and last output
text.serveweb.ts > src/main/diagnostics/index: records each server failure in the Diagnostics log
text.settings-model.ts: Parses settings.json text, resolves values against the registry with problems reported, validates keyboard-shortcut lists, and edits one key in place keeping comments and a parseable result.
text.settings-store.ts: Holds the user settings.json state, writes it atomically through the shared atomic writer, watches it for external edits with bounded re-attachment, notifies change listeners, and reads a single valid setting from a project's .lantern/settings.json.
text.settings-store.ts gotcha: A syntax error keeps the last good values and blocks writes until the file is fixed
text.settings.ts: Persists project languages and providers, dismissed PRs, the local comparisons kept next to them, unfinished mapping runs, whether a project let Lantern add the delegate permission rules, whether the user accepted the VS Code server licence, and the configured Claude executable, loading only the keys it knows.
text.setup-progress.ts: Runs mapping status in a worker and caches progress by project metadata stamp with coalesced concurrent reads.
text.setup-state.ts: Reads progress only when requested or unfinished and clears pending setup after verified chunk completion.
text.skill-scripts.d.ts: Types the detectRtk function, the skill linker check, the project root resolver, the bundled skill lists, the plan format constants and the plan flow reader of the skill scripts that the main process imports.
text.skill-scripts.d.ts < skills/lantern-dele: the skill linker check the panel state comes from
text.extensions.ts < src/main/skills-catalogu: the skill and role counts the linker status line shows
text.extensions.ts < skills/lantern-delegate/: the one check of a linker path, reused for the panel state
turns a typed repo folder into the linker file that is saved
text.skill-scripts.d.ts < src/shared/rtk.ts#R: the status shape detectRtk resolves to
text.skills-catalogue.ts: Lists the skills of a skills repo by role folder, counts its skills and roles for the linker status line, and finds the repo of the configured skill linker, whether the linker is the script or its folder.
text.skills-catalogue.ts < skills/lantern-del: the one check of the linker, whose resolved repo is the catalogue
text.skills.ts: Discovers repository skills with or without group folders, recommends the groups named like a dependency of the project and assumes no group name of its own, lists the skills installed in the project and the user folder, reports Lantern-bundled and local folders per provider skill root, links with a per-name result and git-excludes only the names it linked, takes the catalogue from the repo the user saved and otherwise from the configured skill linker's repo, found again on every call and never saved or published, starts with no checkout path and no remote, so nothing is listed and cloning needs a folder and a remote until the user configures them, reads the remote from the configured checkout's own git config and names none of its own, and clones the remote the user gives (or the checkout's) or fast-forwards the skills checkout, adopting an existing one that has a .git and a SKILL.md within two folders.
text.skills.ts < src/main/skills-catalogue.ts: lists the skills of the repo in use
the repo of the skill linker, used while none is saved
text.state.ts: Stores session state: Claude sessions reconciled from each poll snapshot with a waiting, permission, finished or failed notice (one finished notice for a turn that ends with a background task, none when the task later ends) per transition, or when the same state returns with a newer change time, and Codex sessions from hooks, runner runs and discovery with per-turn deduplication, and says whether a session of a provider can be cleared as finished.
text.state.ts = src/main/codex-turns.ts: turn tracking that drops duplicate and stale Codex events
text.state.ts gotcha: The first poll and the first after a failure notify nothing; a cleared session stays hidden until it changes.
text.subagent.ts: Recognizes subagent events and Claude subagent worktree paths for exclusion from primary-session views.
text.bundle.ts gotcha: A dev run only syncs permission rules and installs no skill or agent, so it never replaces the installed bundle.
text.main.ts = src/main/tray-popover.ts: shows the popover under the tray icon and carries what the page asks for
text.main.ts = src/main/tray-menu.ts: builds the full and compact native tray menus
text.main.ts < src/shared/tray-model.ts#build: turns the project groups into the popover's sections
text.main.ts gotcha: Both data folders are set before the single-instance lock, which is keyed by it; moving them breaks coexistence.
text.lantern-local.ts: Turns a local comparison, the working tree or a branch against a base, into a pull-request-shaped entry with its changed files and per-file reasons, and, for a branch, the reasons, review order, flow, description and plan ticks of its local branch record while that record is not behind the branch, and lists branches, commits and diff totals for choosing one.
text.lantern-local.ts gotcha: Leaves .lantern/ out of every file list and count; a written reason shows only while the file's version matches.
text.lantern-local.ts < src/main/local-reason: generated reasons it merges with written ones
text.lantern-local.ts < src/shared/local-revi: comparison ids, refs and result shapes
text.lantern-pr-remembered.ts: Remembers the pull request records read from remote branches, so one whose branch is later deleted and pruned is brought back, stamped with when it was noticed gone.
text.lantern-pr-parse.ts: Parses and validates PR metadata and the metadata of a local branch record (no id, title or link), safe changed-file paths, optional reasons, reading order, the described sections, the plan items it ticks by the shared plan reference pattern, and the flow checked against the record's own files (dropped with its reason when malformed).
text.lantern-prdiff.ts: Reads bounded diffs for registered PR files and local comparisons, counts of added and removed lines per file of a pull request or local comparison, including untracked working-tree files, and issues revision provenance, with merged-history fallback when the base is unavailable, and for an open PR names the fallback base used or, when none is found, why and which branches can be chosen as the two sides.
text.lantern-prfile.ts: Reads a registered PR file, or a local comparison's file from the working tree or branch tip, bounding text previews and issuing trusted source provenance.
text.lantern-proverlay.ts: Builds and caches localized map overlays for nonremoved files on open PR or local-comparison branch tips, reporting missing records.
text.lantern-prs.ts: Combines local and remote PR records and derives open, merged, or closed status from branch tips and merge history, keeping map-only PRs open until a merge mentions them, then overlays the host's answers (declined, merged by squash, reopened) and details and refreshes them with the origin fetch, carrying the plan items each record ticks, the author and last update read from the branch's own commits (which the host's details replace), and letting a newer record on origin replace an older checked-out copy of the same pull request, while a record whose branch was deleted from origin stays as closed, stamped with when it was noticed gone. The git part of the load is cached per project and reused until a branch tip or a checked-out record changes, so a file read no longer scans every record; a person can ask whether the data changed since the view last took it, or drop the cache.
text.lantern-types.ts: Defines shared graph, language, platform, section, coverage, pull-request, PR description and PR flow data contracts, including the declined state, a flow step carrying the changed files it points at, the plan items a pull request ticks, the plans that load next to the map and the plan files that do not, a file the plan proposes, a pull request that can come from a local comparison, the base branch the host reports for an open one, and a pull request's details from the host or git (author and reviewers with avatars and verdicts, dates, comment and task counts, draft).
text.local-reasons.ts: Asks Claude once for a one-sentence reason per changed file of a local comparison, from a trimmed diff batch sized to the reply cap, and stores the parsed reasons for later lookup.
text.local-reasons.ts gotcha: Kept in the app's data folder, not the project; a reason is retired when the file's version changes.
text.local-reasons.ts = src/main/lantern-loca: file list, versions and revisions of the comparison
text.local-reasons.ts < src/shared/reason.ts#: the rule each reason must follow
text.pr-explain-run.ts: Launches Claude once on Sonnet with no tools from a scratch folder, feeds the prompt on stdin, and ends the run on cancel or after a hard timeout with the reply, capped at the caller's reply size, its usage or a plain failure.
text.main.ts = src/main/lantern-local.ts: adds local comparisons to the map and answers the compare channels
text.tray-menu.ts: Builds the native tray menus: the full one (projects with a state emoji, Open workspace, Clear finished, test cards, Quit) kept for platforms without the popover, and the compact one (Open workspace, Clear finished, Quit) for a right-click on the macOS icon.
text.tray-placement.ts: Places the tray popover under the icon, centred and kept inside the work area of the display the icon is on, shrinking to the room below it and falling back to the top right when the system gives no icon rectangle, and tells whether a click may open it again after a blur closed it.
text.tray-placement.ts gotcha: The icon click blurs the open popover first, so a click soon after it hides must not reopen it.
text.tray-popover.ts: Owns the menu bar popover: a frameless translucent panel under the tray icon that gets the project model once its page is ready, shows when the page reports its height, hides on blur, Escape, a pick or a display change, pushes a changed model while open, and accepts from its own page only a known project path, a known action or a finite height.
text.window-icon.ts: Names the Lantern icon file a window uses on Linux, from the packaged resources or the built assets in a dev run, and none on macOS and Windows
text.windows.ts: Keeps the registry of project windows keyed by real checkout path, creates workspace windows, focuses an existing one instead of a duplicate and opens a window on a --compare review, builds the window-open handler that denies every new window and passes only http and https links to the browser, and locks each workspace window so it navigates only to app pages and attaches only editor webviews on a loopback port without preload or node integration, giving each window the Lantern icon on Linux. Tells its host when no workspace, project or pop-out window is left open, so the app can decide whether to quit.
text.last-window.ts: Decides whether closing the last window quits the app: never on macOS, on Windows unless a tray was created, and on Linux unless a tray was created on a desktop known to host one (KDE, XFCE, Cinnamon, MATE, Budgie, Unity, Pantheon); the handler skips a quit already in progress.
text.webview-permissions.ts: Decides whether the editor webview session grants a permission: only to the loopback editor-server page and the VS Code webview frames it embeds, and adds the microphone policy header to the server's own responses.
text.main.ts = src/main/webview-permissions.t: refuses microphone, camera, clipboard and notification requests from any other origin
text.windows.ts gotcha: Closing a window closes only its own pop-outs; a project window's root is listed only while it is open.
text.windows.ts < src/main/cli.ts: the --project folder and --compare spec of a launch
text.windows.ts = src/main/settings.ts: saves the comparison before showing it
text.windows.ts > src/preload/workspace.ts: tells an open window which comparison to show
text.agent.ts = src/main/auth/spawn-env.ts#ap: adds the project's account credentials to the run's environment
text.main.ts = src/main/auth/credential-serve: starts the credential socket for the user-data folder and closes it on quit
text.main.ts = src/main/auth/credential-socke: places the socket in the profile's folder, or a per-user pipe on Windows
text.main.ts = src/main/auth/known-project.ts: tells the server which opened project a requesting folder belongs to
text.main.ts = src/main/auth/env-names.ts#nam: lists the credential names a project's .env files hold
text.main.ts = src/main/lantern-host-origin.t: tells whether a project is on GitHub or Bitbucket
text.agent.ts < src/shared/languages/index.ts: turns the chosen language into the code a run and its prompt compare by
text.main.ts < src/main/languages/index.ts#re: picks the map and explainer language from the team file, the user's setting, then a fallback
text.lantern-pr-cache.ts: Keeps a result per project root for as long as the git ref state and the checked-out pull request records stay the same, checking that state with a few cheap reads, sharing one load between callers and dropping a root on request.
text.lantern-pr-warm.ts: Loads the pull request data in the background when a project opens and after a fetch, one warm-up per project at a time, works out the revisions of open pull requests ahead of the first diff, revalidates the data when a pull request is entered and drops the cache, fetches and reloads on a Refresh.
text.lantern-host-avatar.ts: Swaps the https avatar links of a pull request's author and reviewers for small inline image data, downloaded with a timeout, a size cap and https-only redirects, cached per link and retried after a failure only once half an hour has passed.
text.lantern-host-avatar.ts gotcha: A person whose avatar cannot be downloaded loses the link, so the view draws initials instead
